parole.significato: abrash (variation or deviation of a colour in Oriental rugs)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish abraş, from Ottoman Turkish ابراش, from Arabic أَبْرَش (ʔabraš, “dappled, mottled”).

parole.significato: a woman or girl of Turkish descent
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish Ayşe, from Arabic عَائِشَة (ʕāʔiša). The use as a common noun is due to the name's commonness among Turkish immigrants, possibly reinforced by the unrelated noun Ische (“gal, chick”).
Borrowed from Turkish kahpe, from Ottoman Turkish قحبه (kahbe), from Arabic قحبة (qaḥba, “whore”). Compare French kahba, cahba.
Borrowed from Turkish tamam, from Arabic تَمَام (tamām).
